newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen up in KGHM wait.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen up in KGHM wait.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the fifth session running and analysts said that after another rise seen on Thursday near-term growth could depend on cash flow after the recent public offering of copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz.

"After the debut of Bank Handlowy we've had growth sessions for several days...and maybe something similar will happen with KGHM," said Stanislaw Kutkowski, a trader at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) SA brokerage.
KGHM starts trade on Thursday. The domestic-investor tranche of its offering last week was 62-percent oversubscribed, the institutional tranche 22-percent.
Analysts said KGHM could start trade around its 21-zloty ($6.4) issue price.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.9 percent to 15,883.1 points and turnover rose 10.3 percent to 160 million zlotys ($48.4 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 78 to 15 with 16 stocks flat.

Analysts said that continued growth by the main WIG index could be limited during the run-up to the September 21 parliamentary elections and that current rises might represent a natural rebound after falls for much of June.
They said the outperformance by small-cap stocks on Wednesday signalled that much of the buying was speculative.
Analysts also said Bank Handlowy could rebound on Thursday and then level out after having falling 2.1 percent on Wednesday, the stock's first fall since starting trade a week ago Monday.
They said electrodes maker ZEW fell 10 percent after news reports the southern town of Raciborz where it is based was particulary hit by the recent flooding.
